ambient: Court astrologer claims unfavorable conjunction. Two horses, no harvest.
A blind monk in a coastal abbey is heard predicting your coronation.
Bandits in the high passes have begun robbing only nobles. Popular.
A pope and an antipope mutually excommunicate each other. Again.
Plague reported in three port cities. Three more port cities deny it.
Emissaries arrive bearing gifts of silk, salt, and several scorpions.
A spice ship runs aground. The cargo is auctioned at four times its weight.
Pilgrims report seeing a comet shaped like a galloping horse.
Mercenary company offers their service to whoever can prove they have coin.
The Khan of the Steppe is said to be 'considering options.' Coastal cities buy candles.
Cartographer presents an updated world map. Twelve cities are misspelled.
Royal mint reports counterfeit coins flooding the markets. The counterfeits are better.
Two princes ride into a forest. One returns. The court does not press the matter.
Heretical text discovered in an abbey library. Two abbots quietly transcribe it.
A camel caravan vanishes between waystations. Survivors carry tea, not goods.
A new translation of an Arabic mathematics treatise reaches Paris. Five priests faint.
Merchant guild seizes a customs house. They issue receipts for everything they take.
Bishops fail to agree on the date of Easter. Easter happens anyway.
Royal falconer found drunk in a tower. The falcon is also drunk.
battle_reports: A messenger arrives at court covered in mud and good news.
The chronicler grimaces. He has only one quill left and the ink is freezing.
Crows gather over a valley to the east. Local farmers stay inside.
A young captain returns missing a horse, a cloak, and one finger.
Banners are taken at a crossroads. Some are kept; some are burned.
backlash: Coalition forming against you in the west. The Pope writes a strongly worded letter.
Mercenaries demand back pay or they will work for whoever defeated you.
Peasant revolt in your interior. Tax collectors arrive home in pieces.
An old enemy returns with new allies. Trumpets sound at dawn over the eastern hills.
Excommunication. Your trade routes north begin asking awkward questions.
A rival sultan publishes your private letters. Most of them are forgeries. The bad ones are real.
